thesis: Land Tax transforms being behind on lands into repeated card advantage and perfect basic-land access, making deliberate restraint a strategic resource.

canonicalIdentity.currentOracleText: At the beginning of your upkeep, if an opponent controls more lands than you, you may search your library for up to three basic land cards, reveal them, put them into your hand, then shuffle.
canonicalIdentity.identityNotes: Original Legends 1994-06-01 credited to Brian Snoddy; printing ID remains from accepted snapshot. Modern Oracle text is not misidentified as original printed wording. Verified focused mechanics source: https://mtg.wtf/card/leg/26/Land-Tax

originalContext.designPurpose: Land Tax makes a player who controls fewer lands capable of collecting up to three basics during upkeep. The reward is cards in hand, not lands on the battlefield or free land drops.

claims.summary: Land Tax has an intervening-if trigger: a rival must control more lands both as upkeep begins and when the trigger resolves. It searches for up to three basic lands and puts them into hand, without granting any additional land play. A one-Plains controller facing two Islands has the required inequality at upkeep.
